column11: p.852 col.1 prints 39 beside 'Lear. How old art thou?'; miun and trent both read 30. Read as 39 by Claude Code on the miun scan, and confirmed by Cliff on the same scan <2026-09-22>.

Corrected <2026-09-22> after Cliff read the review build. The Globe and the Folger read these lines differently: Folger ftln-2307 'To whose hands' ends there, where the Globe's line runs on '...have you sent the lunatic king?' and turns over, so it is a full verse line and cannot be a displaced second half; the earlier row here, folding it with 'Late footed in the kingdom?', came from matching first words only. The page prints 'Speak.' flush at the margin, an unmarked continuation like V.3 250, and Folger ftln-2308 ends with 'Speak.', grouping it with the lunatic-king line. doc/forum.org #lineation/shared-lines-table records the same wrong match by hand and needs correcting. Read by Claude Code on the image <2026-09-22>; `checked` left for Cliff.

p.875: 'Come. [Exeunt Lear and Cordelia, guarded.' then 'Edm. Come hither, captain; hark.'; the count needs the fold here. Folger marks 'Come hither, captain. Hark.' ana=#short (ftln-3281), i.e. standing alone. That is not decisive: across the play the Folger marks a half of 41 of our 233 shared lines #short, including II.1.111 'Is he pursued?' / 'Ay, my good lord.', verified by hand against the page in July. See reports/regenerate-lr-folger-check.tsv. Image p.875 (miun 00000889): 'Come.' is flush but its row is filled to the measure by '[Exeunt Lear and Cordelia, guarded.', so nothing could be set after it; 'Edm. Cliff's decision <2026-09-22>: take the Folger reading. Folger ftln-3550 makes 'Well thought on. Take my sword. Give it the Captain.' one line, so the page's flush row continues it. Note this rests on the Folger's line division, not its @part or its #short tagging, which doc/forum.org #lineation/shared-lines-table does not yet cover. The neighbours corroborate: our 249 'Thy token of reprieve.' and 251 'Haste thee, for thy life.' each stand alone, as Folger ftln-3549 and ftln-3552 (both #short) do. The page alone was ambiguous: the row is flush at the column margin where every other turnover in the play is indented ~2.3u, which had pointed the other way (to a shared half with 'Alb. Haste thee, for thy life.'). Either reading closes the interval. Image p.877 (miun 00000891): 'Thy token of reprieve.' flush and short; 'Edm. Well thought on: take my sword,' at the ordinary indent with the marginal 250; 'Give it the captain.' flush at the margin, the same setting as III.7's 'Speak.' Read by Claude Code on the image <2026-09-22>; `checked` left for Cliff.

p.925 (miun 00000939): 'Eno. [Aside to Agr.] Will Cæsar weep?' / 'Agr. [Aside to Eno.] He has a cloud in 's face.', each at the margin after its aside. Schmidt cites the two together as Ant. III, 2, 51 ('Caesar weep? he has a c. in's face'). The Folger sets them as two lines.

p.925 (miun 00000939): 'So is he, being a man.' / 'Agr. [Aside to Eno.] Why, Enobarbus,' at the margin after its aside. Folger part=I/F; Schmidt cites 'were he a horse' as III, 2, 52 and 'he cried almost to roaring' as 55, which leaves room for one line here. Note: at 'Ant. column11: p.924 (miun 00000938): 'As his strong sides can volley.' / [stage direction] / 'THE SONG.' heading, set in. The Globe counts the heading: Schmidt cites 'can volley' as II, 7, 118 and 'plumpy Bacchus' (the song's second line) as 121, and the page prints 120 beside 'Come, thou monarch of the vine'. The P4's own Globe <lb> numbering also gives the heading a line. In the P4 it is speech text.
